preamble: Numbers in the wordplay of the clues all have something in common and require translation

clue.text: Bird flying out about 7

indicators.note: things sent flying are scattered, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A bird flies off with something to do with the number seven.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble's shared theme is atomic numbers: each number stands for the chemical symbol of that element, so 7 is nitrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a tropical bird famous for its huge, brightly coloured beak.

clue.text: Quiet debauched man set about trapping 18 birds

indicators.note: a trap encloses its catch, so one group of letters is held inside the rest

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: to move things about is to rearrange them, so the letters change places

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute, pleasure-seeking man

explanation.surface: A rowdy, dissipated man quietly sets about catching some birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The rake and the set are mixed up together with argon's symbol caught among them, all after the quiet P. PARRAKEETS is a less common spelling of parakeets.
explanation.definitionFit: Parakeets, also spelt parrakeets, are small long-tailed parrots, so they are birds by example.

clue.text: 56 joining cricket club are cut short at game

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: CC is the standard abbreviation for cricket club
the word with its final letter removed

explanation.surface: A newcomer joins a cricket club and players are reduced to a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At game' reads like a scene, but 'at' is a plain piece of letters and 'game' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game played between a banker and players, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: This writer returned to work with 8 in exploit

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as 'this writer'

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to ply is to work at a trade

explanation.surface: A writer goes back to the office to make use of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxygen's symbol goes inside the word for work, making a stratagem, preceded by the setter turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it, which is what employ means as a verb, as in employing a tactic.

clue.text: English female, loud and unfriendly, squashing 20 with ability to achieve result

indicators.note: to squash something is to press in on it, so one piece is squeezed inside another

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
F is the abbreviation for female
f (forte) is the musical marking for loud
an icy manner is cold and unfriendly

explanation.surface: A loud, hostile Englishwoman crushes something and gets results.
explanation.walkthrough: Calcium's symbol is pressed into the cold word, after three single-letter abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Efficacy is the power to produce an intended effect, the capacity to make something work as hoped.

clue.text: 15 looking embarrassed about wise person making forecast

definitions.note: the answer is a past tense, 'made a forecast'; the clue phrase is looser

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: Someone blushing around a wise prophet as predictions are made.
explanation.walkthrough: The blushing colour wraps around the wise one, with phosphorus's symbol at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foretell or be a sign of what will happen, so presaged means predicted the future.

clue.text: Privileged noble — friend, 85, in east

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A favoured aristocrat with a friend living somewhere in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but is simply its own two letters, before the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A count palatine was a noble with royal powers within his own territory, so a lord holding special privileges.

clue.text: 49 men brought up medical container

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing something up turns it to read from bottom to top

parts.note: OR (other ranks) is a crossword abbreviation for ordinary soldiers, i.e. men

explanation.surface: Some men carry up a medicine case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' suggests carrying the box upstairs, but it turns the soldiers backwards in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: An inro is a small Japanese lacquered case hung from the sash, traditionally used to carry medicines.

clue.text: Journalist, 66, to be in a whirl

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is a stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A frantic reporter is in a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole infinitive phrase, matching the verb sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that eddies swirls round in a circular current, moving in a little whirlpool.

clue.text: Picture 87 obtained by Parisian art firm

parts.note: 'art' is the old English form of 'are', and the French for 'you are' (familiar) is tu es
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A painting acquired by a Paris art dealership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is not painting here but the archaic verb 'thou art'; the Parisian equivalent is French 'es'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting made on wet plaster on a wall or ceiling, a type of picture.

clue.text: Got 29 to come in supporting radical

indicators.note: something that comes in enters and sits inside the rest

parts.note: a red is a left-wing radical

explanation.surface: Someone was persuaded to join a group supporting radical causes.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper's symbol slots between the backer and the leftie.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure is to obtain or acquire something, often with effort, so procured is a synonym of got.

clue.text: Taker of risk with health, adult at home, 62, beset by threat to breathing

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up at home in their sixties faces a menace to their lungs.
explanation.walkthrough: The three short pieces sit inside the strangling thing between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lights one cigarette after another is gambling with their wellbeing, a cryptic description of a heavy smoker.

clue.text: 31 in terribly romantic marriage may be this

indicators.note: one thing in another is included among its letters
something done terribly is badly messed up, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A marriage that is terribly romantic might be described this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sentence frame: the answer completes 'marriage may be ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: A morganatic marriage joins a royal to a commoner, whose spouse and children do not share the royal rank or inheritance.

clue.text: Social-climbing type entertains 74, with everyone getting a drink

indicators.note: a host who entertains has guests within the house, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a snob looks up to those of higher class

explanation.surface: A social climber hosts a party where every guest gets a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Tungsten's symbol is W, from its other name wolfram. A snowball is a British cocktail of advocaat and lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowball is a mixed drink of advocaat and lemonade, popular at Christmas in Britain.

clue.text: Free entries allowing in 92 very hungry

indicators.note: to allow something in is to admit it inside
letters set free are loosened from their order and can rearrange

explanation.surface: Free admission tickets let in a crowd of starving people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free entries' reads as complimentary tickets, but 'Free' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a literary word meaning hungry or greedy, from the Latin for being hungry.

clue.text: Enthusiastic supporter in church always, with 68 joining in

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

indicators.note: someone joining in comes inside the group, so a piece goes within

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A keen fan in church always joins in the singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In church' looks like placement, but the in is part of the surface: church just gives its abbreviation first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerer is one who shouts encouragement, a vocal backer of a team or performer.

clue.text: Posh car carrying daughter behind 47 toys

indicators.note: a vehicle carrying something holds it inside

parts.note: a Rolls(-Royce) is a luxury car

indicators.note: one thing behind another follows it in sequence

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A luxury car takes a daughter and her playthings along.
explanation.walkthrough: Silver's symbol Ag, from Latin argentum, goes first and the daughter follows it inside the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag dolls are soft dolls made of cloth scraps, a traditional children's plaything.

clue.text: Former lover facing endless ordeal, when about 60 stretches out

indicators.note: something without an end has lost its last letter

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: to be about something is to go around it

parts.note: a test is an ordeal; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A former partner, facing an endless ordeal around sixty, drags things out.
explanation.walkthrough: The trial loses its tail and then wraps around the element symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend something is to lengthen or spread it, so extends matches stretches out as a verb.

clue.text: Craftsperson to scowl with girl, 5, getting in the way

indicators.note: things getting in the way are placed in the middle of something

explanation.surface: An artisan frowns at a girl who keeps obstructing the workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl and boron's symbol sit inside the frown after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A glassblower shapes molten glass by blowing through a tube, a skilled maker of handmade items.

clue.text: Beat happy sound with 13 going north

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading upward, from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A rhythm of contented noise travels northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like a musical pulse to go with 'sound', but it is the verb to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: Larrup is a dialect word meaning to thrash or flog, so it is to beat someone soundly.

clue.text: 73 turning up work above

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up flips letters to read from the bottom

explanation.surface: Someone shows up for work upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reads as arriving, but here it flips the symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on the top of, so it is a preposition meaning over or higher than.

clue.text: Pool party after 3

indicators.note: one thing after another follows it in order

explanation.surface: A pool party that kicks off after three o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a lido is a public open-air swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is an outdoor public swimming pool, so it is a kind of pool for bathing.

clue.text: 84 passed ultimately in examination with threefold foundation

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a trial is a test or examination

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter counts

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone finally passed an exam on structures with three legs.
explanation.walkthrough: The symbol and the closing letter go together inside the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripodal describes something resting on three feet or legs, like a tripod's stand.

clue.text: Mark made by pressing 75 into box

indicators.note: pressing something into another pushes it inside

explanation.surface: A dent left by squeezing something into a carton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' suits a crease, ironing in a fold, but here it is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is a line or fold left in cloth or paper, a mark caused by folding.

clue.text: 17 first class in concert that's broadcast

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a prom is a concert, as in the BBC Proms
A1 means first-class; it is written AI with a letter I

explanation.surface: A top-class performance at a concert that goes out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 meaning excellent appears as AI, with the digit read as the letter. The Proms are a famous summer series of London classical concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast news is to announce it widely, which is what proclaim means.

clue.text: Young bird has William, maybe, bowled over after 94

indicators.note: one thing after another follows it in order
something bowled over is knocked head over heels, so it ends up backwards

parts.note: William Tell is the Swiss folk hero, so Tell can be a William

explanation.surface: A chick knocks down a boy called William.
explanation.walkthrough: 'William, maybe' invites a short form like Bill, but the setter wants a surname: Tell, the archer of Swiss legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A pullet is a young hen, especially one less than a year old, so a juvenile chicken.
